newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close up as Bradies reach highs.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close up as Bradies reach highs.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed up as Venezuelan Brady bonds reached record highs amid rising oil prices and the prospect of increased government revenues, traders said.
Rising oil prices have "significantly improved Venezuela's outlook, and that's been reflected in rising debt prices," said Multinvest broker Jose Gregorio Tineo.
With Venezuelan discount bonds VXFLL07oRR setting an all-time high, the positive mood spread to stocks, Tieno said.
The bolsa's 19-share .IBC index moved 0.76 percent ahead to close at 4,664.35 points.

Over eight million shares worth 1.9 billion bolivars ($4 million) changed hands. Investors focused special attention on Electricidad de Caracas, steel producer Sivensa and paper manufacturer Venepal B.
"As Electricidad began to move, that had a positive psychological effect on the market," said Merinvest analyst Boris Molina.
Electricidad closed ahead 1.00 bolivar at 401.00, while Sivensa gained 8.45 bolivars to end at 294.00. Venepal B closed unchanged at 305.00 bolivars as two million shares cross-traded at that price.
Among traded issues, 11 rose, 12 fell and eight closed unchanged. "Discounting the Venepal trade, volume is still shallow," Molina said.
"The oil price rise has brought a torrent of good news to Venezuela, but few foreign investors. How the extra funds will be used is still to be defined," he added.
The government said that it would use some of the windfall revenue from higher-than-expected crude oil prices to meet its outstanding debt payments.
